beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "I've been closing the shop early on Thursdays. Just to sit with the books alone, no interruptions."

options.text: What are you actually looking for when you sit with them?
Sounds like you're avoiding the real work.
Why would the books need quiet to make sense?

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Something in the numbers doesn't add up to what I feel is actually going on. I need the quiet to actually see it."

beats.speaker: reader
beats.text: You turn over the top card.

options.text: That's productive solitude, not avoidance — the details only add up once no one's talking over them.
Closing early is just you slacking off.
This card means you should never work with anyone again.

elaboration: The Hermit's solitude isn't loneliness — it's the deliberate quiet that lets small details finally resolve into a bigger picture.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "My partner thinks I'm pulling away from the business by doing this."

options.text: You're not pulling away — you're finding the next step before you take it.
He's right, you should stop doing this.
What he thinks doesn't matter at all.

elaboration: The Hermit's lantern only ever lights the next step, not the whole road — withdrawing to find that step isn't the same as leaving.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "...Okay. One more Thursday, then I'll actually tell him what I found."
